bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷十六 唐廢帝家人傳第四:
title.en: Volume 16: Family of the Tang Deposed Emperor
title.raw: 卷十六 唐廢帝家人傳第四: Volume 16: Family of the Tang Deposed Emperor

sentences.zh: 廢帝皇后劉氏

translations.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed Later Tang emperor.

sentences.zh: 廢帝皇后劉氏，父茂威，應州渾元人也。

translations.literal: Empress Liu of the Deposed Emperor—her father was Maowei, a man of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, wife of the deposed emperor, was the daughter of Maowei of Hunyuan in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 后為人彊悍，廢帝素憚之。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature fierce and overbearing, and the Deposed Emperor had long feared her.
translations.idiomatic: She was fierce and domineering by nature, and the deposed emperor had always been afraid of her.

sentences.zh: 初封沛國夫人，廢帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: At first she was enfeoffed as Lady of Pei; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was first created Lady of Pei; when the deposed emperor acceded, she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 其弟延皓，少事廢帝為牙將，廢帝即位，拜宮苑使、宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Yanhao had served the Deposed Emperor in youth as a guards officer; when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yanhao was appointed Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Yanhao had served the deposed emperor as a guards officer in his youth; on his accession Yanhao was made commissioner of the palace parks and of the southern court of the Bureau of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年，為樞密使、天雄軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Qingtai 2 he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 2 he was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 延皓為人素謹厚，及貴而改節，以后故用事，受賕，掠人園宅，在鄴下不恤軍士，軍士皆怨。

translations.literal: Yanhao had been plain and honest in character, but once elevated he changed his ways; because of his sister he wielded power, accepted bribes, seized others’ gardens and houses, and at Ye showed no care for the soldiers, so the troops all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhao had been modest and honest, but once he rose in rank he changed his conduct; relying on his sister’s position he took power, accepted bribes, seized gardens and residences, and at Ye neglected the troops, who came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 捧聖都虞候張令昭以其屯駐兵逐延皓，延皓走相州。

translations.literal: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pengsheng command, drove Yanhao out with the garrison troops under his command, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingzhao, chief inspector of the Pengsheng command, expelled Yanhao with the troops stationed under him, and Yanhao fled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，石敬瑭已反，方用兵，而令昭之亂作。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and war was underway when Lingzhao’s mutiny broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang had already rebelled and fighting was under way when Lingzhao’s revolt erupted.

sentences.zh: 令昭乃閉城，遣其副使邊仁嗣請己為節度使。

translations.literal: Lingzhao then shut the city gates and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to request that he himself be made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhao closed the city and sent his deputy Bian Rensi to ask that he be appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 廢帝以令昭為右千牛衞將軍，權知天雄軍府事。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor made Lingzhao General of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor appointed Lingzhao general of the Right Thousand-Bull Guards and acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.

sentences.zh: 已而遣范延光討之，令昭敗走邢州，追至沙河，斬之，屯駐諸軍亂者三千餘人皆死。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent Fan Yanguang to attack him; Lingzhao was defeated and fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and beheaded, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison troops were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Fan Yanguang against him; Lingzhao was defeated, fled to Xingzhou, was pursued to Shahe and executed, and more than three thousand mutinous garrison soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 有司請以延皓行軍法，廢帝以后故，削其官爵而已。

translations.literal: The authorities asked that Yanhao be dealt with under military law, but because of the empress the Deposed Emperor merely stripped him of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officials asked that Yanhao be punished under military law, but because of the empress the deposed emperor only removed his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二子

translations.literal: The Two Sons of the Deposed Emperor
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor’s two sons.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二子，曰重吉、重美，一女為尼，號幼澄，皆不知其所生。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor’s two sons were named Chongji and Chongmei; one daughter became a Buddhist nun, styled Youcheng; none of them is known by whom they were born.
translations.idiomatic: His sons bore the names Chongji and Chongmei; a daughter took vows as a nun under the sobriquet Youcheng. History does not record who bore any of them.

sentences.zh: 廢帝鎮鳳翔，重吉為控鶴指揮使，與尼俱留京師。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor held Fengxiang, Chongji was commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and remained in the capital together with the nun.
translations.idiomatic: While the deposed emperor governed Fengxiang, Chongji served as commander of the Crane-Controlled Guard and stayed in the capital with the nun.

sentences.zh: 控鶴，親兵也。

translations.literal: The Crane-Controlled were the emperor’s personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Crane-Controlled were the sovereign’s personal guard.

sentences.zh: 愍帝即位，不欲重吉掌親兵，乃出重吉為亳州團練使，居幼澄於禁中，又徙廢帝北京。

translations.literal: When the Min Emperor took the throne, he did not wish Chongji to command the personal guard, so he sent Chongji out as regimental commissioner of Bozhou, kept Youcheng within the palace, and also moved the Deposed Emperor to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Min emperor acceded, unwilling to let Chongji command the personal guard, he posted Chongji to Bozhou as regimental commissioner, kept Youcheng in the inner palace, and transferred the deposed emperor to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 廢帝自疑，乃反。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor grew suspicious and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor grew suspicious and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 愍帝遣人殺重吉于宋州，幼澄亦死。

translations.literal: The Min Emperor sent men to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng also died.
translations.idiomatic: The Min emperor sent agents to kill Chongji at Songzhou, and Youcheng died as well.

sentences.zh: 重美，幼而明敏如成人。

translations.literal: Chongmei from childhood was bright and keen like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Chongmei had been clever and quick-witted from childhood, like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，自左衞上將軍領成德軍節度使、兼河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，改領天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，封雍王。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Chongmei rose from General of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently Grand Guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor acceded, Chongmei advanced from general of the Left Guard to military governor of the Chengde Army, concurrently grand guardian of Henan and overseer of the Six Armies and all guards; he was then transferred to military governor of the Tianxiong Army, made grand councilor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭反，廢帝欲北征，重美謂宜持重，固請毋行。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Deposed Emperor wished to campaign north; Chongmei said he should act with restraint and firmly begged him not to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the deposed emperor wanted to march north; Chongmei urged caution and firmly pleaded that he not go.

sentences.zh: 廢帝心憚敬瑭，初不欲往，聞重美言，以為然，而劉延皓與劉延朗等迫之不已，廢帝遂如河陽，留重美守京師。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor inwardly feared Jingtang and at first did not wish to go; hearing Chongmei’s words, he thought them right, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others pressed him without cease, so the Deposed Emperor went on to Heyang and left Chongmei to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor feared Jingtang and at first did not want to march; hearing Chongmei, he agreed, but Liu Yanhao, Liu Yanlang, and others kept pressing him, so he proceeded to Heyang and left Chongmei to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師震恐，居民皆出城以藏竄，門者禁止之。

translations.literal: The capital was shaken with terror; residents all left the city to hide, and the gatekeepers forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was gripped by panic; residents fled the city to hide, and gatekeepers tried to stop them.

sentences.zh: 重美曰：「國家多難，不能與民為主，而欲禁其避禍，可乎？」

translations.literal: Chongmei said: “The state is in great difficulty; we cannot act as masters for the people, yet would forbid them to flee harm—can that be right?”
translations.idiomatic: Chongmei said, “The realm is in grave trouble; we cannot protect the people, yet would forbid them to escape disaster—how can that be right?”

sentences.zh: 因縱民出。

translations.literal: He therefore let the people leave.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore allowed the people to go out.

sentences.zh: 及晉兵將至，劉皇后積薪于地，將焚其宮室，重美曰：「新天子至，必不露坐，但佗日重勞民力，取怨身後耳！」

translations.literal: When the Jin army was about to arrive, Empress Liu piled firewood on the ground and was about to burn the palace halls. Chongmei said: “When the new Son of Heaven comes, he will surely not sit in the open; this would only later overburden the people’s strength and win resentment after death!”
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin army neared, Empress Liu heaped firewood to burn the palace. Chongmei said, “When the new emperor arrives he will not sit in the open air; this would only waste the people’s labor later and bring hatred after our deaths!”

sentences.zh: 后以為然。

translations.literal: The empress thought him right.
translations.idiomatic: The empress agreed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝自焚，后及重美與俱死。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor burned himself; the empress and Chongmei died with him.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor set himself afire; the empress and Chongmei perished with him.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 家人之道，不可不正也。

translations.literal: The way of the "Family" cannot fail to be set right.
translations.idiomatic: The norms that govern household and kin must be upheld.

sentences.zh: 夫禮者，所以別嫌而明微也。

translations.literal: Now ritual is that whereby one separates what is suspect and makes clear what is subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual exists precisely to dispel doubt and bring fine distinctions to light.

sentences.zh: 甚矣，五代之際，君君臣臣父父子子之道乖，而宗廟、朝廷，人鬼皆失其序，斯可謂亂世者歟！

translations.literal: Extreme! At the time of the Five Dynasties, the way of lord and lord, minister and minister, father and father, son and son went awry; at the ancestral temple and at court, both the living and the dead lost their proper order—this may indeed be called an age of chaos!
translations.idiomatic: How far things had fallen! In the Five Dynasties the reciprocal duties of ruler and ruled, father and child, collapsed together; temple and palace alike were scenes where neither men nor shades kept their station—truly an era of disorder!

sentences.zh: 自古未之有也。

translations.literal: From antiquity onward there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like it appears in the earlier record.

sentences.zh: 唐一號而三姓，周一號而二姓。

translations.literal: Tang bore one reign title but three surnames; Zhou bore one reign title but two surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The house called Tang ruled under a single dynastic name yet passed through three clans; the house called Zhou did the same with two.

sentences.zh: 唐太祖、莊宗為一家，明宗、湣帝為一家，廢帝為一家；

translations.literal: Tang Taizu and Zhuangzong were one family; Mingzong and the Min Emperor were one family; the Deposed Emperor was one family;
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang thus falls into three bloodlines: Taizu and Zhuangzong; Mingzong and the short-reigned Min emperor; and the deposed emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 周太祖為一家，世宗為一家。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu was one family, Shizong was one family.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou likewise splits in two: the line of Taizu and that of Shizong.

sentences.zh: 別其家而同其號者，何哉？

translations.literal: They distinguish their families yet share the same dynastic name—why is that?
translations.idiomatic: Why, then, does the chronicle cleave the clans yet leave the dynastic label unchanged?

sentences.zh: 唐從其號，見其盜而有也；

translations.literal: For Tang, following its name shows that they stole it yet came to possess it;
translations.idiomatic: For Later Tang the shared name exposes naked usurpation: each claimant seized the throne from the last.

sentences.zh: 周從其號，與之也。

translations.literal: for Zhou, following its name means it was given to them.
translations.idiomatic: For Later Zhou the single title marks legitimate succession: the mandate was handed down within the alliance that founded the state.

sentences.zh: 而別其家者，昭穆親疏之不可亂也。

translations.literal: But distinguishing their families is because senior and junior generations, close and distant kin, cannot be confused.
translations.idiomatic: The separate "families" preserve the temple order of fathers and sons, near kin and far—lines that must not be blurred.

sentences.zh: 號可同，家不可以不別，所以別嫌而明微也。

translations.literal: The name may be the same; families cannot fail to be distinguished—this is to separate suspicion and clarify the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic names may repeat; agnatic lines may not. That, again, is the work of ritual: clearing doubt and marking fine shades.

sentences.zh: 梁博王友文之不別，何哉？

translations.literal: The Prince of Bo of Liang, You Wen—why was no family distinction drawn for him?
translations.idiomatic: Why, then, does the Later Liang record leave Bo Prince You Wen outside the neat partition of "families" that I have just defended?

sentences.zh: 著禍本也，梁太祖之禍，自友文始，存之所以戒也。

translations.literal: It is to write down the root of calamity: the calamity of Liang Taizu began with You Wen; keeping this unresolved exists in order to warn.
translations.idiomatic: Because the historian means to expose the taproot: the founder of Later Liang brought ruin on himself starting with You Wen, and the deliberate ambiguity in the record is itself the lesson for posterity.
